# Signet Verify

> Age verification on a website usually means collecting ID or sending users
> off to a third-party checker. signet-verify is a browser SDK that checks a
> cryptographic age credential from the Signet app instead, without the site
> ever seeing personal data.

For websites that need to gate content by age range (adult content, age
brackets for minors) without running their own verification flow. A single
function call opens a modal, waits for a signed response on a same-origin
`BroadcastChannel` (no relay connection), and checks both the credential and
the issuing verifier's professional registration. The package contains the
listener only: nothing in it posts that response, and `verifyAge` does not
expose the request ID a sender needs, so a real user cannot reach
`verified: true` until you wire up a same-origin sender of your own.

## Getting Started

```bash
npm install signet-verify
```

```javascript
import { verifyAge } from 'signet-verify';

const result = await verifyAge('18+');
if (result.verified) {
  // user confirmed 18+ by a confirmed professional verifier
}
```

This resolves with `verified: true` only after a same-origin sender posts a
valid `signet-verify-response` message for the call. Otherwise the modal keeps
waiting and the call resolves with `error: 'timeout'` after 120 seconds, or
`error: 'cancelled'` if the user closes it.

For a script tag / CDN build, use the IIFE export (`signet-verify/iife`),
which exposes `window.Signet`, for example
`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/signet-verify@0.7.2/dist/signet-verify.iife.js`.

## Key Concepts

- **Credential, not identity**: the proof carries an age range and verifier
  info, never a name, date of birth or other PII.
- **Verifier confirmation**: by default a result only counts as `verified`
  when the issuing verifier is checked against a public professional
  register (GMC, SRA, TRA, etc.) via a verification bot; this can be relaxed
  with `acceptUnconfirmed` or pointed at a different bot with
  `verifierCheckUrl`.
- **Same-browser vs cross-device**: `verifyAge` covers the modal flow and
  receives its response on a `BroadcastChannel` named
  `signet-verify-<requestId>`; it makes one network request, to the
  verification bot, and never connects to a relay (its `relayUrl` option is
  only written into the request object). The message it accepts is
  `{ type: 'signet-verify-response', requestId, credential, subjectPubkey }`
  (the `VerifyResponse` type from `signet-protocol`; `subjectPubkey` is not
  read), where `requestId` is the 32-character hex ID generated for that call
  and `credential` is a signed kind-30470 Nostr event whose tags include
  `tier`, `age-range` and `entity-type` (and optionally `expires`). The README
  has the full field list and how each failure maps to an error code.
  `waitForAuthResponse` is the
  lower-level cross-device primitive for a consumer that mints its own
  challenge and waits on a relay for the signed response; only it needs a
  relay that serves kind-1059 gift wraps to an unauthenticated reader.
- **The sign-in deadline**: a cross-device wait has one deadline,
  `issuedAt + AUTH_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SEC`. `issuedAt` must be passed on every
  call for the same sign-in, including retries after the page was
  backgrounded, or the relay query anchor is wrong.

## API Surface

- `verifyAge(requiredAgeRange, options?) => Promise<SignetVerifyResult>`:
  the same-browser modal flow. `requiredAgeRange` must be one of
  `'0-3'`, `'4-7'`, `'8-12'`, `'13-17'`, `'18+'` and is matched exactly.
  Failures are reported in `result.error`, not as a rejection.
- `waitForAuthResponse(options) => Promise<SignetAuthResult>`: the
  cross-device primitive. It resolves on success and rejects with an `Error`
  whose `message` and `code` are the failure code (`expired`, `timeout`,
  `denied`, `aborted`, `relay-refused`, and others listed in the README).
  Options: `requestId`, `relayUrl`, `sessionPrivKey` (a 32-byte
  `Uint8Array`) and `expectedOrigin` are required; `issuedAt` (unix
  seconds), `timeout` (milliseconds), `since` (unix seconds) and
  `abortSignal` are optional. The README has the full option and result
  tables.
- `AUTH_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SEC` (`300`, seconds), `DEFAULT_RELAY_URL`
  (`'wss://nos.lol'`): constants used to compute and check the sign-in
  deadline.
- Result and option types: `SignetVerifyResult`, `SignetVerifyOptions`,
  `WaitForAuthOptions`, `SignetAuthResult`, `SignetAuthEvent`.
